newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down in jittery market.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down in jittery market.

text.p: *Peso average at 26.318 from 26.297 to the dollar
The Philippine peso closed lower on Wednesday at 26.323 against the dollar from 26.304 in a market made jittery by recent steep declines in interest rates, traders said.
Talk that foreign funds were leaving the country due to the low interest rates caused by Friday's cut in reserve requirements spurred banks to cover their short dollar positions, traders said.
And the planned phasedown of the foreign exchange cover for oil imports had led banks to be wary, traders said. The cover is currently at around 60 days and will be eliminated by March 1.
"Banks are just going to be a little long but they don't think they'll be short," a local bank dealer said.
The uneasiness in the market was further compounded when the Central Bank raised its offer rate for the dollar at 26.33 from an earlier quote of 26.32 early in the day, traders said.
Still, a dealer said banks remained cautious as trades stayed below the Central Bank's dollar offer rate.
The peso only hit a day-low of 26.326 after opening at its day-high of 26.305. Turnover swelled to $215.50 million from $191.50 million.
"Currently, offshore funds have adopted a wait-and-see attitude," a foreign bank dealer said. "If interest rates go lower, arbitrage money will be going out."
